ai_summary: Great Britain is currently generating 3.7 GW of wind power, with Scotland delivering an estimated 2.4 GW, which represents 23.8% of installed Scottish wind capacity. Driven by this renewable output, Scottish carbon intensity stands at 0 gCO2/kWh, presenting a stark contrast to the GB-wide carbon intensity of 210 gCO2/kWh. However, structural transmission bottlenecks continue to limit the transfer of clean power southwards. As a consequence, 849 MWh of Scottish generation has been curtailed so far today through Balancing Mechanism bids, incurring a constraint cost of about £47,969. To replace this curtailed renewable volume, an estimated 161,329 m3 of gas was burned elsewhere on the network, releasing 297 tonnes of additional CO2. Extrapolating today’s figures yields an estimated total yearly cost of £18 million for Scottish curtailment. Apportioned across Great Britain's total annual electricity demand, this constraint mechanism is estimated to add approximately £0.06/MWh to UK electricity invoices, underscoring both the economic impact on consumers and the carbon consequences of existing grid limitations.
